decoder.statusNormalization: state/string; eventTime=receivedTime, clockStatus=unverified, coverage=unknown, quality flag event_time_is_receive_time, senderEventId=null; no historical sender-time assertion

read_settings.result: unknown-command-outcome; sanitized discovery snapshot may be retained separately

save_settings.successEvidence: SaveOK proves save/readback only; requiresRestart remains pending

restart.successEvidence: Restarting is response only; no proof of completed reboot; timeout/disconnect ambiguous

runtimeInvariants: Capabilities declare adapter design, never proof of installed runtime or hardware conformance.
Both HTTP and MQTT share this composite profile; MQTT does not carry count in the inspected firmware.
HTTP enabled requires countChannels nonempty and httpToken; MQTT enabled requires credentials; all-disabled is invalid.
Unique nodeId and signalId bindings, source ownership, definition observed_delta numeric, and immutable mapping are checked by RegistryManagement and writer.
Namespace/hardwareSerial are routing aliases under authenticated ACL, never company authorization.
Same namespace+serial may not bind multiple authenticated sources; enrollment verifies registry credential, not serial-derived password as trust proof.
Status has no sender event ID/time: no exactly-once historical status guarantee; do not invent one using receive UUID.
Reject duplicate form/JSON keys, contradictory aliases, unbound node_id and invalid types; decode form once.
Setting names, scalar types, ranges, editability, dependencies and secret flags require validated firmware metadata; JSON schema alone does not authorize writes.
Never log full settings responses; redact secret values before runtime observation, public API, receipt and audit persistence. Private values are vaulted separately.
Generic command parameters must not contain a secret setting; secret updates use a separately scoped private reference/config workflow before command dispatch.
save_settings rejects duplicate setting names, unknown/unvalidated metadata and oversized complete encoded frames before publish.
Fragment assembly limitation in current firmware remains: no response or a truncated response is not success. Discovery/write capability remains unverified until isolated conformance tests.
Retained replies and unsolicited snapshots do not confirm a fresh request. Matching seqId/response_to is necessary where available; no durable firmware command dedup is claimed.
A stale executor may not publish mutation after losing its lease; physical exactly-once cannot be guaranteed by database fencing alone. Ambiguous mutations are unknown without blind retry.
Profile export is a manual firmware configuration checklist and validated values, not a claim that unchanged firmware accepts a new generic JSON config import.
Firmware buffer retention, loss on full queue, sample interval and binary version remain hardware capabilities requiring tests; no unconditional three-day durability claim.
